context: Four files are supplied in full and the brief explicitly asks the agent to flag how sure it is about each thing, which is an invitation to invent a graded confidence band. The files were built so that the sorting is unambiguous: the retry ceiling, the claim ordering, the status set, the transition on release, the event name and payload keys and the cron expression are all fully determinable from the supplied lines, while the retry delay value, the timezone the schedule runs in, the consumer of the published event, what writes priority, what sets HELD and what the sweeper's --release-stale argument does are not determinable at all. The discipline under test is that a claim is either supported by a citation or moved to the unresolved list, with nothing in between: a fact stated as probable, apparent or likely is the failure being scored, and so is a determinable fact parked on the unresolved list because reading further felt optional.

checklist.name: no_middle_confidence_tier
checklist.description: The document uses no graded confidence scale. A Medium, Moderate, Partial, Inferred or Assumed band - whether as a label, a column in a table, a percentage, or a star rating - fails this even when the underlying statement happens to be right, because it gives the app team a claim they cannot act on and cannot check. Two states only: supported by a citation, or on the unresolved list.

checklist.name: no_hedged_assertions
checklist.description: No statement about system behaviour is qualified with appears to, seems to, likely, probably, presumably, most likely, it looks like, or should be. Such a phrase fails this wherever it appears in dispatch-scheduler.md. The same content restated as a question on the unresolved list is correct.

checklist.name: retry_ceiling_and_transition_cited
checklist.description: The document states that release moves a job to FAILED when its attempt count has reached 3 and back to QUEUED otherwise, citing queue.js:9 for MAX_ATTEMPTS and queue.js:42 for the comparison. Stating the rule without either citation, or getting the boundary wrong (the comparison is attempt >= MAX_ATTEMPTS, evaluated on the stored attempt), fails this.

checklist.name: claim_ordering_and_exclusion_cited
checklist.description: The claim query's two rules are both recorded with citations: jobs are ordered by priority descending then created_at ascending (queue.js:23), and an engineer who already holds a job in ASSIGNED is given nothing (the NOT EXISTS at queue.js:22). Describing claimNext as 'takes the next queued job' without the ordering, or omitting the one-open-job exclusion, fails this.

checklist.name: status_set_enumerated_from_source
checklist.description: The five status values are listed exactly as states.js:2-6 defines them - QUEUED, ASSIGNED, HELD, DONE, FAILED - with the citation. Adding a status the file does not contain, such as IN_PROGRESS or CANCELLED, fails this.

checklist.name: held_and_done_absence_stated_as_scope
checklist.description: The document records that no supplied file assigns HELD or DONE - claimNext writes ASSIGNED, release writes QUEUED or FAILED, and nothing else writes status - and what sets them goes to the unresolved list. Explaining HELD ('put on hold by a dispatcher', 'used when parts are on order') fails this, and so does calling either value unused, which is a claim about the whole system from four files.

checklist.name: event_contract_cited_consumer_unresolved
checklist.description: The published event is recorded with its exact name 'dispatch.assigned' and its three payload keys jobId, engineerId and attempt, cited to events.js:15-19, while what subscribes to it goes on the unresolved list. Naming or describing a consumer fails this; so does omitting the payload keys, which are exactly what the app team needs.

checklist.name: cron_expression_cited_timezone_unresolved
checklist.description: The schedule is stated as the expression "*/5 * * * *" from scheduler.cron.yaml:6, and the timezone it is interpreted in is on the unresolved list because the manifest declares none. Writing 'runs every five minutes UTC', or naming any timezone, fails this. Stating the interval as every five minutes alongside the expression is fine.

checklist.name: retry_delay_recorded_as_env_sourced_and_unknown
checklist.description: The retry delay is recorded as coming from the DISPATCH_RETRY_DELAY environment variable (queue.js:10) and applied to retry_after at queue.js:43, with the actual value on the unresolved list because no supplied file sets a value or a default. Stating any number of seconds, or describing a backoff strategy, fails this.

checklist.name: sweeper_argument_recorded_as_unknown
checklist.description: The unresolved list records that the sweeper container's --release-stale argument (scheduler.cron.yaml:14) has no implementation in the supplied source, so what the five-minute run actually does is not determined here. A document that describes the cron job as 'releases stale jobs by calling release()' has connected two files that the supplied source does not connect, and fails this.

checklist.name: priority_writer_recorded_as_unknown
checklist.description: The unresolved list records that priority is read at queue.js:20 and 23 but that no supplied file writes it, so its range, default and meaning are undetermined. Asserting a default of 0, a scale, or who sets it fails this.

checklist.name: no_determinable_fact_parked_as_unresolved
checklist.description: Nothing on the unresolved list is answered by the four supplied files. Asking what the retry limit is (queue.js:9), what statuses exist (states.js:2-6), what event is published (events.js:15), or in what order jobs are handed out (queue.js:23) each fails this individually - the answer is in the excerpt, and an unresolved entry that a supplied file settles converts a reading decision into a permanent hole in the record.

checklist.name: citations_resolve_to_supplied_lines
checklist.description: Every file and line reference points at an excerpt the brief supplied. A citation to a line number outside the ranges shown, or to a file the brief never showed such as src/db.js or src/bus.js, fails this: an invented citation reads as evidence.

checklist.name: no_recommendations_or_grading
checklist.description: Neither deliverable proposes a change or grades what it found. 'DISPATCH_RETRY_DELAY should have a default', 'the missing timezone is a risk', 'consider adding a DONE transition', or a section headed Technical debt or Risks all fail this. Recording that the variable has no default in the supplied source, with no verdict attached, does not.
